about: The golden fixture for encrypted calls (docs/calls.md §Keys, §Signaling, §Ringing;
mls/core/src/call/): the key schedule off the MLS exporter, the AES key the WebRTC
frame-encryption layer derives from a sender key, the signaling codec and its two lanes,
Written by an independent implementation (a separate Python generator, not in this repository: Python's
hmac/hashlib, a hand-written protobuf encoder, the cryptography package, and ring
expectations written out by hand from the spec), so the Rust replay is a
second opinion. Replayed through the fixture door (kind "call") in Rust, JavaScript
and Swift (and, in Peachy's Android client, Kotlin). Each case has exactly one of
`expect` or `expectError` (a substring of the refusal's message).

The server replays a recorded Left: the second copy is refused (the D3 attack).
A sender's stamps strictly increase; each one moves the mark.
Two sends that crossed on the way are both accepted, and each only once.
A member claims leaf 3 with a stamp 120 s ahead: it takes that stamp only, and the leaf's own later frames are accepted.
A stamp is remembered until the clock bound refuses it, and is refused as stale after.
One sender's mark says nothing about another's.
The same stamp in another call is another frame.
A receiver with no mark (it just joined, or restarted) still refuses a recording more than 120 s old; exactly 120 s is accepted.
A stamp more than 120 s ahead of the receiver's clock is refused, so no stamp can push a mark further ahead than that; exactly 120 s is accepted.
A newer epoch's leaf may be another device with another clock: its mark starts again, and the older epoch's frames are refused after it.

Older than 60 s: recorded missed, nothing rings.
A stale non-ringing notice is nothing at all.
The caller's clock 120 s ahead of this device's still rings (the skew is inclusive).
Dated more than 120 s ahead of this device's clock: recorded missed, nothing rings.
Dated as far ahead as the codec allows, so that no clock would ever call it stale: missed.
Fresh by the server's clock, and 180 s old by the caller's: still rings.

An age more than the skew below zero is no clock's: recorded missed.
The same offer twice changes nothing.

Another member answering a group ring does not stop mine.
60 s of ringing: missed.
A timer for another call changes nothing.

Cancelling before an answer.

Hanging up a 1:1 ends it for both.
Leaving a group call is just leaving.
A group caller who leaves before anyone joined cancels the ring, so nobody rings into an empty room.
Once someone joined, the caller leaving is just leaving: others may still join.
A member who joined someone else's call never cancels that caller's ring.
A group above the ring cap rang nobody, so there is no ring to cancel.
Nothing to hang up.
Both called at once; the larger call id keeps its call.
The smaller call id ends its own call with normal and rings for the other.
Equal call ids: end mine and answer busy.
Already in a 1:1 and the same person calls again: the old call is over and the new one rings.
A redelivered or replayed offer for a call in this device's history rings nothing.
A replayed old offer while ringing is not a second caller: no busy reply.
A Hangup for a call this device is not on is handed back to keep, by call id.
A Hangup for a different call while one rings is kept too; the ring goes on.
Its caller already hung up: a missed call, never a ring.
My own device already answered it: answered elsewhere, never a ring.
My own device already declined it (a 1:1 decline reaches my devices as itself).
Another member leaving a group call does not end its ring.
The kept Hangup says how it ended, ahead of the Offer's age.
